near_miss.lead: eat and drink merism: Arm. owtem ew əmpem ~ Gk πῖνε καὶ ἦσθ' (*h₁ed- + *peh₃-)
near_miss.why_not: Both Armenian passages are Gospel/Exodus quotations (Luke 5:30, Exod. 32:6), and 'eat and drink' is a universal pairing; nothing ties the Armenian wording to Od. 16.141 beyond the generic merism.

anchors: xcl:MH_1_2_13_Lazar_Parp ed. page 2377 - PDF page 177 (word id 63662) (w2/2)
near_miss.lead: naming formula: dat. relative + 'name' + 'was': Arm. orowm anown ēr ~ Gk τῷ οὔνομα ἦν (*h₁nómn̥ + *h₁es-)
near_miss.why_not: Exact cognates in the same construction, but this is an everyday naming idiom, and Armenian prose of this period follows Greek (biblical ᾧ ὄνομα) syntax closely, so a calque cannot be excluded; not distinctive phraseology.

anchors: xcl:MH_1_2_13_Lazar_Parp ed. page 2382 - PDF page 182 (word id 65096)
near_miss.lead: numeral 'five' + 'year': Arm. hing ... am ~ Skt pañcamīm ... samām (*penkʷe, *sem-h₂- 'year/summer')
near_miss.why_not: Arm. am and Skt samā are genuine cognates, but numeral + year is counting language, not a formula; the contexts (Noah's 500 years vs. Arjuna's fifth year) are not congruent.

anchors: xcl:MH_1_2_13_Lazar_Parp ed. page 2374 - PDF page 174 (word id 63168) (w2/2)
near_miss.lead: 'day' + 'tears': Arm. awr əst awrē artasowacʻ ~ Gk νύκτάς τε καὶ ἤματα δάκρυ χέουσα (*h₂eh₂mr̥, *dáḱru)
near_miss.why_not: Armenian has 'day by day' (a Christian homiletic idiom on penitential tears) and no night/day merism or 'pour' verb; the Homeric line is a lament formula. Shared nouns only.

search_lead.slab_anchor: xcl:MH_1_2_13_Lazar_Parp ed. page 2359 - PDF page 159 (word id 57422)
search_lead.cognate: none (wording renewed throughout; Arm. ayr 'man' < *h₂nḗr only)
search_lead.argument: Heroic gnome 'for a brave man it is better to show his worth for one day and die than to live long in disgrace' (Arm. kʻaǰi ar̄n ... law ē mi awr ... ew mer̄anel). Same structure in Ajax's 'better to perish once (ἕνα χρόνον) or live' than to be ground down at length (Il. 15.511), in Laxdæla's 'better to get short honour than long disgrace', and (recalled, not found in the search) Beowulf 2890-91 'deað bið sella eorla gehwylcum þonne edwitlif'. It is thematic only, with no cognate lexemes, so it is not a phraseological claim.
